title: How the closing reference moves
subtitle: Foresight by checkpoint, movement half-life, pregame absorption, and overreaction by bucket -- measured, not explained
abstract: This paper measures four properties of the devigged closing price, the reference forecast used across the site, without attributing any of the movement to a cause. First, a market foresight premium (MFP) series shows how much resolving power the reference carries over a scoreboard-only model at successive in-game checkpoints, per bit of remaining uncertainty: reference skill is positive at all ten MLB checkpoints, model skill is negative at five of them, and MFP reads 0.051 at checkpoint 1 (n=3,589) and 0.0159 at checkpoint 9 (n=1,110), its lowest reading. That series was rebuilt on 2026-09-17 from the segment-clean corpus, and revision 1's climb to 0.5208 is withdrawn. Second, a half-life estimate shows how many hours before start half of a sport's measured pregame line motion has occurred: 2.75 hours for international soccer, 3.67 for MLB, 4.76 for NBA, with tennis and WNBA censored at the coarsest measured boundary (">6.0"). Third, a bucketed breakdown of that same pregame motion shows where it concentrates in time, sport by sport. Fourth, a moved-to-price-versus-outcome test, bucketed by move size and rebuilt on 2026-09-16 from the segment-clean tick corpus, shows the moved-to price sitting 0.03 to 0.0642 above the eventual outcome rate in MLB (n=555 to 19,044) and 0.2671 to 0.3184 below it in international soccer (n=11 to 3,564); revision 1 of that table, computed on the joined corpus, read 0.0518 to 0.0801 and -0.1945 to -0.3648 on roughly three times the rows. The four instruments do not share one observation window.

blocks.text: The devigged closing price is CourtVision's reference forecast, and before it closes it moves. This paper asks four measurement-only questions about that movement: how much resolving power the reference carries over a scoreboard-only model at each in-game checkpoint; how many hours before start a sport's pregame price finishes half its measured motion; where in time that motion concentrates; and how a just-moved-to price compares with the outcome eventually realized, bucketed by move size.

Each measurement below comes from one artifact, already published as a module on the analytics site. This paper restates their per-checkpoint, per-sport and per-bucket numbers in one place, with the denominators attached, and repeats what each artifact's own novelty note says about the instrument.

blocks.label: Status
blocks.text: Revision 1 of this paper quoted artifacts computed on the joined in-game corpus (78,986 MLB ticks, artifact as_of dates up to 2026-07-25), in which one stored tick file could hold ticks from more than one real game and carry another game's outcome label. Those values are withdrawn. Both in-game tables below now quote the segment-clean corpus -- 27,351 MLB ticks across 178 stored games and 4,265 soccer_intl ticks across 27, of which 26,677 MLB and 3,383 soccer ticks fall inside the published checkpoints -- the overreaction table as_of 2026-09-16 and the foresight-premium table as_of 2026-09-17, receipt mlb-ingame-timing-regeneration.json. Every number that moved is a population change, not forecaster improvement: no forecaster changed; the removed rows carried another game's label. Nothing quoted here is under review any longer. The half-life and absorption instruments read a separate scraped line-history feed and are untouched.

Four artifacts back this paper, and each carries its own observation window or none at all; they are not pooled. novel_market_foresight_premium.json holds a market foresight premium (MFP) series at successive in-game checkpoints for two sports: ten MLB innings (checkpoint n from 46 to 3,589) and nineteen international-soccer minute marks in 5-minute steps (checkpoint n from 33 to 402). MFP compares the reference's resolving power and a scoreboard-only model's, each relative to a naive baseline, and divides the gap by the reference's remaining entropy in bits (floored at 0.15 bits). It is composed from info_arrival_curve.json and market_convergence.json and publishes an as_of of 2026-09-17 but no observation window. Both inputs are revision 2 on the segment-clean corpus -- info_arrival_curve.json rebuilt 2026-09-16, market_convergence.json 2026-09-17 -- so the series no longer mixes revisions.

novel_line_half_life.json holds one half-life estimate per sport -- the hours before start by which half of that sport's total measured pregame line motion has occurred -- for the five sports that cleared a 20-pregame-move-pair floor. The estimate is built from four coarse minutes-to-start buckets (6h+, 3-6h, 1-3h, 0-1h) and linear interpolation to the 50 percent point. It reads a scraped line-history feed dated 2026-07-25 and publishes a per-sport window rather than one shared span, each ending 2026-07-17: 30 days for MLB and NBA, 29 for international soccer, 15 for tennis and 14 for WNBA, one file per day.

micro_absorption.json holds the same underlying per-series consecutive-snapshot devigged-probability movement, broken into the same four minutes-to-start buckets, with n_series_used, n_pregame_snapshots, n_move_pairs, and a median snapshot interval reported per sport. It is the direct source for the half-life artifact's bucket totals, is dated 2026-07-25, and carries the same per-sport windows, so only these two artifacts share a window.

market_overreaction.json holds, for MLB and international soccer only, five move-size buckets (0-1pt, 1-3pt, 3-6pt, 6-10pt, 10pt+) each carrying n, the price the market moved to (moved_to_price), the outcome rate eventually realized (outcome_rate), and their difference (moved_to_minus_outcome). It was rebuilt on 2026-09-16 from the segmented in-game corpora, which it now names alongside an as_of, where the withdrawn revision published neither; it still publishes no observation window, so its rows cannot be placed on the half-life artifact's calendar.

This paper restates published numbers; it computes nothing beyond the same-artifact difference already labeled moved_to_minus_outcome in market_overreaction.json. The defining expressions of the four instruments, as documented in their own artifacts, are:
G(h) = cumulative absolute movement from far-to-near / total absolute movement; half_life = h where G(h) = 0.50 (linearly interpolated)
moved_to_minus_outcome = moved_to_price - outcome_rate, within one move-size bucket

The half-life and absorption bucket totals are built from summed ABSOLUTE per-snapshot moves, not net price travel: a price that moves up and back down contributes to the total the same as a price that moves once and stays. This is stated in the half-life artifact's own declared_confounds and is carried through to every half-life and absorption number in this paper.

Checkpoint foresight, MLB. Table 1 lists all ten MLB checkpoints, rebuilt on the segment-clean corpus. Reference skill is positive at all ten, so the reference beats the naive baseline throughout; model skill is negative at checkpoints 1 to 4 and at 10 but positive from the 5th inning through the 9th, where the scoreboard-only model catches up. MFP -- the reference's resolving-power gap over the model, normalized by remaining reference entropy -- no longer rises through the game. It reads 0.051 at checkpoint 1, sits between 0.0831 and 0.181 from the 2nd inning through the 8th, and collapses to 0.0159 at checkpoint 9 as the two forecasters converge. The 0.411 at checkpoint 10 (extra innings, n=46) is the series maximum and a thin tail, not a tenth step. Revision 1's climb to a peak of 0.5208 depended on the joined corpus and is withdrawn.

Table 3 gives the same underlying per-sport series and snapshot counts, split into the four minutes-to-start buckets used to build the half-life estimate above. NBA's final-hour bucket carries the largest single-bucket mean absolute move of any sport-bucket pair in this table (0.00117), about seventeen times its own 6h+-bucket value (0.00007); every other sport's final-hour value is smaller relative to its own early-window value.

blocks.label: Caution
blocks.text: Every row in this table moved when the corpus was re-segmented, and none of that movement is the market or the model behaving differently. MLB's gaps shrank (the 0-1 point bucket from 0.0689 on 66,697 rows to 0.0302 on 19,044) and soccer's grew (the same bucket from -0.1945 on 7,791 rows to -0.2837 on 3,564), because the rows carrying another game's outcome label were dropped. Within revision 2 the thin rows still need care: the international-soccer 6-10 point bucket rests on 11 observations, and the 10pt+ bucket, which now shows the largest gap in either sport at -0.3184, on 57. Neither carries the weight of the 3,564-observation 0-1 point bucket.

sections.heading: Robustness and what would falsify this

items: The market foresight premium's own novelty note grades it INCREMENTAL: the paired model/market/naive instrument is a published Kalshi/NBA method, and only the per-bit normalization is claimed as unpublished (novel_market_foresight_premium.json prior_art_verdict, prior_art_citation).

The half-life packaging is graded NOVEL_PACKAGING, not a new phenomenon: only the single per-sport half-life constant is fresh packaging (novel_line_half_life.json prior_art_verdict, prior_art_citation).

The overreaction bucket test is graded INCREMENTAL against a published cross-sport study and a published in-play soccer study; the contribution is applying the same instrument at consecutive-row grain to the corpora held here (market_overreaction.json novelty.verdict, novelty.closest_prior_work).

Half-life and absorption totals sum ABSOLUTE per-snapshot moves, so they measure price churn, not net travel; a back-and-forth sequence inflates the same total one large repricing would (novel_line_half_life.json declared_confounds).

Tennis and WNBA are censored, not zero: their 50-percent crossing falls past the 6-hour boundary of the coarsest bucket, so ">6.0" is the most specific statement available (novel_line_half_life.json results[].half_life_label, crossing_in_open_bucket).

The MLB checkpoint-10 foresight row (extra innings) carries n=46, nearly two orders of magnitude below the largest checkpoint (n=3,589); its MFP of 0.411, the highest in the series, is a thin-sample estimate (novel_market_foresight_premium.json results.mlb.checkpoints[]).
Model skill is positive at checkpoints 5 through 9, so MFP's late fall is the model closing on the reference, not the reference weakening (info_arrival_curve.json checkpoints.mlb).

The four instruments do not share an observation window: the half-life and absorption artifacts read one scraped feed with a per-sport span (14 to 30 days, each ending 2026-07-17), while the foresight-premium and overreaction artifacts read the in-game tick corpora and publish no window at all (novel_line_half_life.json results[].observation_window; micro_absorption.json observation_window).

Both in-game tables are revision 2, rebuilt a day apart (overreaction 2026-09-16, foresight premium 2026-09-17), and the rebuild moved every MFP row: info_arrival_curve.json now reports 1,110 MLB ticks at the 9th-inning checkpoint where the withdrawn revision reported 2,282.

The market foresight premium mixes real information the market prices with plain misspecification of the single state-only model used as the model_skill baseline; an MFP above zero shows only that this particular model trails the reference at that checkpoint.

The half-life and absorption instruments cover one scraped window per sport (14 to 30 days, each ending 2026-07-17), not a full season; neither the foresight-premium nor the overreaction artifact publishes an observation window.

The overreaction bucket test compares a moved-to price against a realized outcome rate at consecutive-row grain, not at independent game-level grain, so bucket n overstates the number of independent observations behind each rate.
None of the four artifacts records what caused a given price move, only that a move of a given size happened at a given time; nothing here should be read as a claim about why prices move.
The international-soccer 6-10pt overreaction bucket (n=11) and the MLB checkpoint-10 foresight row (n=46) are reported for completeness, not as reliable standalone estimates.
Both in-game tables are revision 2 on the segment-clean corpus and neither is under review, but they were rebuilt a day apart and still publish no observation window.

sections.heading: How to read this on the site

blocks.text: The calibration inspector (inspector id calibration) carries the checkpoint-level model-market gap and entropy series behind the foresight-premium table above, published as the analyses market-convergence-by-checkpoint and market-disagreement-brier-by-bucket. The devigged-movement-by-time-to-close analysis restates the same per-series snapshot movement used to build the half-life and absorption tables here, at the same four minutes-to-close buckets; no finer checkpoint view of that movement is published.

The novel_market_foresight_premium, novel_line_half_life, micro_absorption, and market_overreaction modules publish the charts and the full per-sport, per-checkpoint, and per-bucket arrays this paper's tables are drawn from, including what was left out for space (all 19 international-soccer checkpoints, and the kbo/npb/domestic-soccer exclusions noted in Tables 2 and 3). The in-game join-integrity finding, linked below, records which artifacts were rebuilt and when.

limitations: The market foresight premium mixes real market information with plain misspecification of the single comparison model, and cannot separate the two.

The half-life and absorption instruments cover one scraped window per sport (14 to 30 days, all ending 2026-07-17), and the foresight-premium and overreaction artifacts publish no observation window at all, so the four instruments are not on one timeline.
The overreaction bucket rows are built from correlated consecutive-row observations within games, not independent game-level draws, so bucket n overstates independent support.
No artifact records why a price moved; this paper states when and by how much, never a cause.
The smallest rows in this paper (international-soccer 6-10pt overreaction bucket, n=11; MLB checkpoint-10 foresight row, n=46) are reported for completeness, not as reliable standalone estimates.

Both in-game tables are revision 2 on the segment-clean corpus and neither is under review, but they were rebuilt a day apart and publish no observation window, so neither can be placed on the half-life artifact's calendar.
